## Research directions

::: {.theme-grid}
::: {.theme-card}
<div class="theme-label">Current research</div>

### Climate risk measurement

How definitions, aggregation, spatial scale, and temporal scale change what we infer about heat exposure and climate risk.

**Examples:** Jensen gaps, metric-dependent heat-season timing, heat-event structure, physiological heat strain.
:::

::: {.theme-card}
<div class="theme-label">Methods</div>

### Systems & quantitative modelling

I am interested in representing interacting components, feedbacks, heterogeneity, infrastructure, and vulnerability using statistical, network, agent-based, and simulation approaches.

[Earlier modelling projects →](/research/#systems-and-quantitative-modelling)
:::

::: {.theme-card}
<div class="theme-label">Direction I am building toward</div>

### Adaptation & mitigation planning

Quantitative models that connect climate hazards and exposure to interventions, constraints, trade-offs, and policy choices—with the goal of supporting adaptation and mitigation decisions.
:::
:::

::: {.approach-callout}
### Modelling approach · normatively grounded quantitative modelling

I do not treat metric definitions, thresholds, aggregation scales, objective functions, or the populations represented by a model as purely technical defaults. These choices can encode normative and political judgments about **whose risk is measured, which harms count, and which trade-offs are made visible**. My aim is to make those choices explicit, examine their consequences quantitatively, and carry that reflexive approach into systems models for climate adaptation and mitigation.
:::

## Selected findings

::: {.result-grid}
::: {.result-card}
<div class="result-number">≈ 7 weeks</div>

### Heat metrics can agree hourly and disagree seasonally

Over the Indo-Gangetic Plain, temperature- and WBGT-defined 90-day heat windows differ by about seven weeks in the median, despite strong hour-to-hour comovement.

[Metric-dependent heat timing →](/projects/wbgt-utci/)
:::

::: {.result-card}
<div class="result-number">E[f(X)] ≠ f(E[X])</div>

### Aggregation can change measured heat risk

Nonlinear heat metrics and threshold exceedances can acquire systematic, spatially structured biases when high-resolution climate data are averaged too early.

[Mind the Jensen Gap →](/projects/jensen-gap/)
:::

::: {.result-card}
<div class="result-number">1980–2024</div>

### Heat is changing in timing, persistence, and recovery

I examine whether heat seasons are beginning earlier, ending later, lasting longer, and providing shorter breaks between events across India.

[Heat-event timing →](/projects/heat-event-timing/)
:::
:::
